extracted.intended_audience: academics, researchers, and technical communicators who participate in or are affected by peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Observational guidance and commentary about academic peer review processes, reviewer behaviors (the 'Reviewer 2' phenomenon), and expectations for reviewers and authors in research journals and conferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of peer review is to ensure that a piece of writing or research meets the standards of a given publication or publisher as well as any accepted quality or implementation conventions of relevant scholarly fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer review evaluates fit with venue standards and disciplinary conventions; its audience is usually limited to editors and the author(s), not the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-blind peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: double-blind peer review: the authors do not know the identity of their reviewers and vice versa
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common form in research venues; anonymity can lead to reviewers being referred to by numbers (e.g., Reviewer 1, Reviewer 2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-blind peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: single-blind: authors do not know the identity of their reviewers, but the reviewers know the identity of the author(s)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Widely used; preserves reviewer anonymity but not author anonymity, which can affect reviewer behavior and conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors and reviewers are made aware of each other’s identities; this is often called “open peer review”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open review reduces anonymity and may change the tone and content of feedback compared with blind models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and audience of peer reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review feedback is often shared only with prospective authors and personnel at a given publication venue; unlike public reviews, peer review work often has an audience limited to editors and the author(s), and reviewers usually remain anonymous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because reviews are typically confidential and reviewers anonymous, this structure shapes reviewer candor and the potential for unmoderated negative behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good-faith, expert evaluation and helpful critique
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review is intended to be (and in many cases actually is) expert evaluation and helpful critique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-quality reviewers take time and effort, provide clear, constructive comments, and aim to help authors improve their work rather than to attack or self-promote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid vitriol, self-promotion, and bad-faith commentary
rubrics_metrics.description: The peer review process can open the door for all types of unmitigated vitriol, self-promotion, and general bad-faith commentary among what is intended to be expert evaluation and helpful critique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should avoid personal attacks, promotional self-citation, and comments that serve the reviewer's agenda rather than the integrity of the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer should read the submission carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide feedback that demonstrates careful reading; avoid feedback that suggests the reviewer did not, in fact, read the piece very carefully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surface-level or inaccurate criticisms indicate poor review quality; reviewers are expected to engage substantively with the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid prescriptive demands to adopt reviewer’s own work
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend that the author read what the author suspects is Reviewer 2’s own research on the topic and revise the entire piece accordingly (with a tone that expresses sufficient awe for Reviewer 2’s work).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While pointing to relevant literature is appropriate, reviewers should not use reviews to force authors to reorient their work toward the reviewer's priorities or to unduly promote the reviewer's publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware double-blind failure modes (reviewer identifying author’s work)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend that the author read the author’s own research and revise accordingly (this is one of the more entertaining potential outcomes of the double-blind peer review process).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In double-blind contexts, reviewers identifying and privileging the author's prior work undermines anonymity and can produce incoherent or unfair requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid requesting contradictory revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask for absolutely contradictory revisions (the actual implementation of which could potentially create a rhetorical paradox that results in the universe collapsing in on itself).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors and reviewers should be mindful of consistency across requests; contradictory guidance is unhelpful and places authors in an impossible position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid excessive or opportunistic revision demands
rubrics_metrics.description: Torment an author with revision requests even when the reviewer asked the author to submit the piece in the first place while knowing perfectly well that the author was super busy and had a million other things to do.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should tailor revision requests to genuine improvements and refrain from piling on unnecessary work as a form of gatekeeping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition that reviewers invest time, care, and skill
rubrics_metrics.description: It takes considerable time, care, and skill to review what is often dense and detailed information (to the point where folks have published on what it takes to be a good referee).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer review is labor-intensive professional service; assessments of review quality should factor in the expertise and effort required.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-quality referees provide clear, helpful comments to improve manuscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: There are many reviewers who go above and beyond in generating clear, helpful comments designed to help authors improve their work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the standard to emulate: actionable, specific, and constructive feedback focused on improving clarity, argument, evidence, and fit to venue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review commonly produces conflicting reviewer recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Often one reviewer in the mix will be enthusiastically supportive of a piece while another will rip it apart if not outright reject it; for reasons that are part of the great mysteries of the universe, the latter is somehow always (just ask any researcher) Reviewer 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and editors should expect and manage reviewer disagreement; editorial synthesis is necessary to produce consistent decisions and clear revision guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monetary compensation and professional service expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Monetary compensation for peer review work often ranges from nothing to very little; for academics it is considered part of the 'professional service' component of their workloads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because peer review is often unpaid, recognition, workload accounting, and norms around service are relevant for sustaining quality reviewing practices.
